newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel traded at $25.90/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel traded at $25.90/bbl.

text.p: The comatose jet fuel market was resuscitated on Thursday with the sale of one cargo and a bid by a major, both at healthy levels relative to recent low prices, traders said.

The 100,000-barrel cargo was sold by a Chinese trader to a US trader at $25.90 per barrel for April 29-May 3 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis. This was the first deal seen since March 3 when a European major sold to a Singapore trader at $28.50.
Prices have since slumped as buyers stayed away due to the current low demand season with an offer seen early this week at a low $25.30 per barrel, fob.

The major bid for the same volume of jet fuel at $26.10 for April 18-22 lifting fob. Traders said some market players believe that the recent physical jet/gas oil spread of around minus $2.00 per barrel was too wide.

While jet fuel demand elsewhere in Asia was soft, the Indian subcontinent was providing some support. Nepal has bought 30,000 tonnes of kerosene from Mitsubishi Corp at $204 per tonne, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis. Nepal also bought diesel from
Glencore at $194 per tonne, c-and-f for May 1-10 deliveries.

Sri Lanka has bought 80,000 barrels of jet fuel at 20 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and 200,000 barrels of diesel at a 39-cent premium for April 21-22 delivery, c-and-f. Sri Lanka seeks another 80,000 barrels of jet fuel and 220,000 barrels in a tender for May 5-6 delivery.

Glencore appeared to have a stranglehold on the Indian subcontinent as it is also favourite to win Bangladesh's tender to buy 155,000 barrels of jet fuel with its offer of $1.48 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes for April 22-24 delivery, c-and-f.
India's kerosene tender for May closes today and India was expected to take three cargoes late on Friday, unike the one cargo per month in its previous two tenders for March and April.
After a two-day absence, the Singapore trader who has so far bought nearly seven million barrels of gas oil in one month, purchased another 300,000 barrels in two cargoes on Thursday.
The trader bought one cargo from a Mediterranean trader at $26.80 a barrel for April 29-May 3 lifting fob, and a cargo from another local trader at $27.50 for April 18-22 lifting fob.

Traders said the Singapore trader's continued buying spree helped to maintain the strength of gas oil prices despite lower swaps prices for May which shaved off 40-50 cents to $25.20/$25.30 a barrel, spooked by lower gas oil futures values in London.
Traders said the Chinese market remained quiet, as buyers were put off by the high Singapore prices.
The last deal was seen last week when a cargo was sold at $206 per tonne, c-and-f, when prices appeared to have softened. But the market has since picked up again, traders said.
